name: The Sacred Flame
summary: At Splithoof Hold, Rau Cliffrunner seeks to silence the Galak centaur's sacred fire. With blessed water, you enter their stronghold, quench the brazier, and take the Cloven Hoof.

sections.title: Striking the Hearth
sections.body: North of Freewind Post, Splithoof Crag marks the heart of Galak territory in Thousand Needles. Deep in its cavern, Splithoof Hold, a fire burns that the centaur hold sacred. Rau Cliffrunner prepares an etched phial of purified water for his allies. You enter the hold, use the water to quench the flame for a moment, and take the Cloven Hoof relic guarded within.

sections.title: Secrets of the Hoof
sections.body: When Rau Cliffrunner sees the Cloven Hoof, its strange power stirs his mystical senses. Tauren scholars have long fought the marauding centaur tribes across Kalimdor. The relic hints at deeper forces, still poorly understood, that feed the centaur's zeal and tribal unity.

faq.q: Where is the sacred flame located?
faq.answer: The flame burns deep inside Splithoof Hold, a cavern in the centaur camp at Splithoof Crag, north of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Who asks you to douse the flame?
faq.answer: Rau Cliffrunner, an elder stationed high atop Freewind Post, asks you to douse the flame after investigating the Galak centaur.

faq.q: How do you put out the flame?
faq.answer: Use the Filled Etched Phial Rau Cliffrunner provides. It holds water gathered earlier in the chain, and briefly quenches the brazier.
The Cloven Hoof is a revered tribal relic kept inside the flame by the Galak centaur. Rau Cliffrunner senses unusual magical energy from it and hopes to learn about centaur culture and power.

faq.q: Why do the tauren want this relic?
faq.answer: Centaur tribes have driven tauren from their ancestral hunting grounds for generations. Taking a sacred heirloom disrupts Galak operations while the tauren seek to understand the arcane or spiritual forces behind their enemies' savagery.

faq.q: Which centaur clan guards Splithoof Hold?
faq.answer: The Galak tribe controls Splithoof Crag and its cavern hold. They are the chief centaur clan on the floor of Thousand Needles canyon.

angles.text: As a tauren, striking into a centaur den and taking its sacred icon answers generations of raids. The relic is also a valuable prize for the scholars at Freewind Post.
As a shaman, you can sense the strange energies radiating from the Cloven Hoof. They show that the centaur draw on mystical forces beyond brute savagery.
